choices.response: Nara is an older capital. Try the city you are in.
Fuji is a mountain. Look at the city name.
Kamakura was a different seat of power.

moreInfo.title: Edo
moreInfo.text: Edo became the political center of the Tokugawa shogunate. During the Meiji transition it was renamed Tokyo.

title: Konbini Roulette
intro: Find one food or drink nobody has tried.
task: Buy it. Everyone tastes it. Rate it together from 1 to 5.
hint: Look for rice triangles, egg sandwiches, hot snacks.
reveal: This is how a megacity eats at odd hours. Not a snack stop. A system.

title: Machine Hunter
intro: Some machines sell drinks. Hunt for a stranger one.
task: Find the strangest vending machine or vending-machine product you see.
reveal: The city stays open after the staff go home. The machines keep working.

title: Millions of Quiet People
intro: A packed train can still be quiet.
task: On a busy train, notice what people do so they do not disturb each other.
reveal: Tokyo trains work because people share the quiet, not only because of the rails.

title: Something Is Watching Shinjuku
intro: Something huge is hiding above street level.
task: Find the enormous creature before anyone points it out. Photograph it.
reveal: Godzilla. The head sits above the Shinjuku Toho Building in Kabukicho.

moreInfo.title: Kaiju
moreInfo.text: Godzilla began as a film about fear and the sea. The head on this building is a shop-sign and a local joke.

title: How Do You Control This?
intro: Shinjuku Station moves a city through a building.
task: Find two design tricks that help huge numbers of people move through the station.
observeWhat: Colours, numbers, floor marks, queues, sounds.
reveal: Marks, numbers and queues do the shouting so people do not have to.

title: The Giant
intro: Three famous towers. Only one is this tall.

choices.response: Famous, but shorter than this one.
Close, and red. Look at the new one.
Yes. This is the tall one.

title: Find Old Tokyo
intro: New Tokyo is under your feet. Old Tokyo is still in view.
task: Find the direction of Asakusa and Sensō-ji below.
reveal: From here you can see old Tokyo and new Tokyo at the same time.

title: Why Doesn't It Fall?
intro: A tower this tall has to live with earthquakes.
task: How can something this tall survive strong movement?

question.text: How can something this tall survive strong movement?

choices.response: Rigid towers fight the ground. This one is meant to move a little.

choices.text: It can absorb and control movement
choices.response: Yes. It is built to sway and settle.
It is meant to stay standing.

reveal: Tokyo Skytree uses modern structural damping. A reinforced-concrete central column moves somewhat independently from the outer structure, helping reduce earthquake motion.

moreInfo.title: Named after a pillar
moreInfo.text: The designers named the concept in reference to the central pillar found in traditional five-story pagodas. That is a name for the idea, not a claim that ancient pagodas supplied this engineering solution.

title: Don't Understand Anything
intro: Do not explain the rooms yet.
task: For the first ten minutes, do not explain the art. Just walk. Then each person picks: most beautiful, strangest, most alive.
reveal: Keep those three picks. Kyoto and Osaka will ask what changed.

title: Is It Still the Same Art?
task: If this moving experience were frozen into one photograph, would it still be the same artwork?
